intro: Vocabulary for driving, fines, breakdowns and road safety.
p.autopista.consejo: It is a big road for fast driving. You can go «por la autopista» or be «en la autopista».
p.carril.consejo: In Spain you drive in the right-hand lane. To overtake, you use the left one.
p.paso de cebra.consejo: It is called «de cebra» because of its stripes. Drivers must let pedestrians cross.
p.multa.consejo: The verbs are «poner» and «pagar» a multa. You say «me han puesto una multa por aparcar mal».
p.atasco.consejo: You also say «tráfico» or «retención». You say «estar en un atasco».
p.gasolinera.consejo: It comes from «gasolina». There you «echar gasolina» or «repostar».
p.cinturón.consejo: It is compulsory to «abrocharse el cinturón». It is also the one you wear at your waist.
p.taller.consejo: The ll sounds like y: ta-YER. A «taller mecánico» repairs cars.
p.seguro.consejo: As an adjective it means «without danger»: «es seguro». As a noun, it is car or home insurance.
p.adelantar.consejo: It also means doing something earlier: «adelantar trabajo». On the road, look before overtaking.
p.frenar.consejo: It comes from «freno», the part that stops the car. You brake with your foot.
p.pinchar.consejo: A «pinchazo» is a flat tyre. You say «se me ha pinchado una rueda».
p.grúa.consejo: It takes away badly parked or broken-down cars. On a building site, the «grúa» lifts heavy things.
p.aparcar.consejo: In Spain you say «aparcar» and in America «estacionar». It is spelled «aparqué» with qu.
b1.texto:
Useful verbs: **conducir**, **adelantar**, **frenar**, **girar** and **aparcar**. **Abrocharse el cinturón** is fastening your seat belt; **llevar el carné de conducir** is carrying your driving licence.

On the road there are **carriles**, **semáforos** and **pasos de cebra** for **peatones**. The general maximum speed for cars on a motorway is 120 km/h, unless a sign shows a lower one.

There may be **atascos**; **multas** can be given for speeding or bad parking; a tyre can get a puncture (**pincharse**) and a car can run out of petrol. If it breaks down, call **la grúa** or **el seguro** and take it to **el taller**.

Rules use impersonal forms: **no se puede adelantar**; **está prohibido aparcar**; **hay que ceder el paso a los peatones**; **es obligatorio abrocharse el cinturón**. And for what happens by accident: **se me pinchó una rueda**, **se nos acabó la gasolina**.
b2.f2.texto: There was a huge traffic jam on the motorway.
b2.f4.texto: No, a lorry got a puncture.
b2.f5.texto: That is why they closed a lane.
b2.f6.texto: Well, yesterday I was fined for parking on a zebra crossing.
b2.f7.texto: Did the tow truck take your car?
b2.f8.texto: Yes, but my insurance covers the repair.
b4.texto:
There are three very common resources on the road:

- **General rules**: **es obligatorio**, **está prohibido**, **no se puede** or **hay que** + infinitive. **Es obligatorio abrocharse el cinturón.**
- **What happens by accident**: **se** + **me / te / le / nos / os / les** + verb. The verb agrees with what breaks or runs out. **Se nos pinchó una rueda.**
- **Someone you do not name**: the third person plural. **Me pusieron una multa.**
b4.e0.texto: It is compulsory to fasten your seat belt.
b4.e1.texto: We got a puncture on the motorway.
b5.f0.texto: The motorway stretches straight under a leaden sky.
b5.f1.texto: The cars move slowly like a line of red lights.
b5.f2.texto: Inside the car, Lucía taps the steering wheel with her fingers.
b5.f3.texto: The radio repeats an old song without stopping.
b5.f4.texto: In the distance shines the sign of a petrol station.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly, the brake lights come on in front of her.
b5.f6.texto: Lucía brakes hard and stops a metre from the lorry.
b5.f7.texto: Her heart beats fast in her chest.
b5.f8.texto: A stopped lorry shows a flat tyre next to the barrier.
b5.f9.texto: A man in a yellow vest places orange cones in the right lane.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That is it! A «multa» is the money you pay for breaking a rule.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Insurance is paid regardless; it is not a penalty for bad parking.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A «carril» is a strip of the road, not something you pay.
b6.pregunta: What do you pay if you park where it is forbidden?
b7.o0.refuerzo: The participle does not complete this rule: an infinitive is needed.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes! After «es obligatorio» comes an infinitive: «abrocharse».
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is a conjugated verb, not an infinitive.
b8.frase: A un camión se le pinchó una rueda
b9.o0.refuerzo: The petrol station sells petrol, but it does not repair breakdowns.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The «grúa» is a vehicle that carries cars, not a place to go.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! At the «taller» they repair cars.
b9.pregunta: Where do you take a broken-down car?
b10.frase: Se nos ____ una rueda en la autopista.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! It agrees with «una rueda», which is singular.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It is plural, but only one tyre has gone.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The subject is the tyre, not us. We only suffer the puncture.
b10.pregunta: Which word does the verb agree with?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Stopping is halting. «Adelantar» is passing another vehicle.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Adelantar» is getting ahead of a slower vehicle.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Turning is changing direction. «Adelantar» is passing another car.
b12.pregunta: What does «adelantar» mean on the road?
b13.frase: Mi ____ cubre la reparación del coche.
b13.o0.refuerzo: A «carril» is part of the road; it does not cover costs.
b13.o1.refuerzo: A «atasco» is stopped cars; it pays nothing.
b13.o2.refuerzo: Yes! Insurance pays for damage when there is a problem.
b13.pregunta: What covers the costs of the car?
p.pinchó.consejo: From «pinchar», to puncture. The accent is on the «ó».
p.cortaron.consejo: From «cortar», to cut. Here, to block a road.
p.pusieron.consejo: From «poner», to put. The stress is on «sie».
p.abrocharse.consejo: Use it with «cinturón» to say buckle up.
p.exceso.consejo: Excess is more than what is allowed.
p.plomo.consejo: It is the same word as the metal lead; here it means a dull, heavy grey.
p.avanzan.consejo: From «avanzar», to move forward. The «z» sounds like «th».
p.parado.consejo: It describes something that is not moving.
p.pinchada.consejo: From «pinchar», to puncture: the tyre has lost air.
p.barrera.consejo: A barrier blocks the road or the way.
p.chaleco.consejo: A bright vest that helps others see you on the road.
p.conos.consejo: Plural of «cono», a pointed shape used on roads.
p.vehículo.consejo: Any means of transport on wheels, like a car or a van.
